author: Emma McCorkindale
title: East Longmeadow school resource officer catches break-in suspect - NewsBreak
text:
By Emma McCorkindale ,
12 hours ago
EAST LONGMEADOW, Mass. (WWLP) – A Springfield man has been charged following a break‑in that East Longmeadow police traced through home surveillance footage.
Lubavitcher Yeshiva Academy hosts Wild West themed Purim celebration The East Longmeadow Police Department states that on Tuesday at 12:15 p.m., a resident located on Speight Arden reported that they could see someone breaking into their home over their surveillance camera system. Officers were sent to the area and found evidence that confirmed that the home had been broken into.
A resident from Elm Street reported a short time later that a suspicious-looking man was seen running through their backyard, looking like he was trying to hide. A school resource officer went to the area and located the suspect in the backyard, who matched the description of the person seen on camera from Speight Arden.
After a short chase on foot, the suspect was captured. The missing property from the home on Speight Arden was found in the backyard on Elm Street. The homeowner also confirmed to officers that the suspect was someone who was known to them.
The suspect, 43-year-old John Loranger of Springfield, was arrested and charged with breaking and entering in the daytime with intent to commit a felony, malicious destruction of property over $1,200, and larceny from a building. He is scheduled to be arraigned in Palmer District Court on Wednesday.
